commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Rename to Jiji and implement greet and exit
Level-1: Implement interactive echo and bye exit
Level-2: Implement add and list functionality
Level-3: Implement Task class and mark/unmark commands
Level-4: Implement Todo, Deadline, and Event task types
Level-5: Implement OOP exception hierarchy and comprehensive edge case tests
Level-6: Implement delete command with A-Collections
Docs: Update User Guide in docs/README.md and add doc maintenance rule in AGENTS.md

commitResults.messageBody:
Task data exists only in memory during runtime and is lost whenever
the application terminates.

Users need their tasks and completion states to persist across sessions
so that they can track tasks over time.

Let's,
* add file storage in data/jiji.txt using a pipe-delimited format
* save tasks to disk automatically whenever the list is modified
* load saved tasks on startup and restore their completion states
* handle corrupted lines gracefully by skipping invalid records

A simple text file with delimiter formatting keeps data human-readable
and requires no external database dependencies.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement date and time parsing and formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event date/time inputs are treated as raw text strings
without validation or formatted presentation.

Users benefit from standard date parsing and human-friendly display
formats to easily recognize deadlines and event schedules.

Let's,
* introduce DateTimeUtil to parse LocalDate and LocalDateTime
* format date outputs to readable representations (e.g. MMM dd yyyy)
* standardize stored dates in data/jiji.txt using ISO formats
* update Deadline and Event classes to format dates and times

Using java.time APIs provides type safety and ISO standard compliance
for date handling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use enums for command types and task categories
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands and task storage categories rely on magic string literals and
string matching logic dispersed across multiple methods.

Using raw strings reduces type safety and makes command dispatching
and task type handling error-prone.

Let's,
* create CommandType enum to represent valid user commands
* create TaskType enum to encapsulate task storage type codes
* refactor command loop in Jiji.java to switch over CommandType
* refactor task deserialization in loadTasks to use TaskType

Enums enforce compile-time type safety and provide a cleaner foundation
for object-oriented command dispatching.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor codebase into dedicated OOP components
commitResults.messageBody:
Jiji.java coordinates I/O, file storage, task mutations, and parsing
within a single monolithic class, violating SRP.

A modular architecture decouples concerns, simplifies future extensions,
and establishes standard OOP design patterns.

Let's,
* extract Ui class for console interaction and formatting
* extract Storage class for file persistence and load/save operations
* extract TaskList class to encapsulate task collection mutations
* extract Parser class and implement Command pattern hierarchy
* refactor Jiji.java to serve purely as an application coordinator

Separating responsibilities into dedicated classes improves cohesion,
testability, and maintainability.

All Java source files reside in the default root package under
src/main/java without modular package structure.

Organizing classes into domain packages enhances modularity, enforces
access boundaries, and establishes standard project conventions.

Let's,
* create jiji root package for application entry point
* create jiji.command package for Command hierarchy and types
* create jiji.task package for Task models and TaskList collection
* create jiji.storage package for file persistence
* create jiji.ui package for console interface
* create jiji.parser package for Parser and DateTimeUtil
* create jiji.exception package for domain exception classes

A clean package hierarchy prevents namespace clutter and facilitates
future build automation and testing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Configure Gradle build automation for Jiji
commitResults.messageBody:
Building, running, and packaging the application relies on manual javac
and java command lines without build automation.

Automating project tasks with Gradle streamlines builds, dependencies,
execution, and cross-platform packaging.

Let's,
* merge add-gradle-support branch providing Gradle wrapper scripts
* configure build.gradle application mainClass to jiji.Jiji
* set shadowJar artifact output name to jiji.jar
* enable interactive standard input in Gradle run task
* update User Guide with Gradle execution instructions

Gradle establishes standardized build lifecycle tasks for compilation,
automated testing, and deployment.

Automated verification currently relies solely on end-to-end UI script
tests without granular unit tests for core domain classes.

Adding automated unit tests ensures individual methods behave as
expected and guards against regressions during refactoring.

Let's,
* add DateTimeUtilTest for date/time parsing and formatting methods
* add ParserTest for valid commands, missing arguments, and syntax
* add TaskListTest for collection mutations and edge case indexing
* add TodoTest for task state transitions and file format output

JUnit 5 tests can be executed automatically during Gradle builds.

Users and evaluators require clear instructions to package and run
the application as a standalone executable JAR across platforms.

Providing step-by-step shadowJar generation and invocation commands
simplifies distribution and manual verification.

Let's,
* verify shadowJar builds standalone executable jiji.jar
* test java -jar execution and working-directory persistence
* update User Guide with standalone JAR packaging and run commands

Packaging via shadowJar enables running Jiji independently without
local Gradle or IDE dependencies.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot search for specific tasks by keyword and must manually
scan the entire task list.

Implementing a find command allows users to quickly filter and locate
tasks matching a search term in their descriptions.

Let's,
* add FIND to CommandType enum
* create FindCommand to query TaskList and render matching items
* implement case-insensitive findTasks method in TaskList
* add showMatchingTasks formatting in Ui
* update Parser to recognize find command syntax
* add unit and UI test coverage for find operations
* update User Guide with find command syntax and output

The find command enhances task retrieval and list navigation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc documentation across all classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Source code contains several unannotated constructors, enum constants,
and unescaped JavaDoc markup tags that fail javadoc generation.

Adding comprehensive header comments and standard JavaDoc annotations
ensures clean API documentation and eases developer onboarding.

Let's,
* add class and method-level JavaDoc comments to all source files
* document all CommandType and TaskType enum values
* add private constructor documentation for utility classes
* escape HTML formatting brackets in task storage descriptions
* verify clean javadoc generation via Gradle

Comprehensive JavaDoc comments meet SE-EDU documentation standards.

The codebase should formally document and comply with SE-EDU coding
standards for formatting, naming, and structure.

Standardizing coding conventions ensures clean readability, consistent
code style, and eases ongoing maintenance.

Let's,
* create seedu-java-coding-standard skill with conventions guide
* update AGENTS.md instructions to mandate coding standards
* enforce explicit utility class construction and encapsulation
* verify 4-space indentation and brace formatting across codebase

Adhering to SE-EDU coding standards ensures uniform code quality.
